title.value: Information Gain Sampling for Active Learning in Medical Image Classification
title.justification: The main focus and theme of the paper centers around proposing and evaluating an information-theoretic active learning framework applied to medical image classification tasks.
title.quote: This work presents an information-theoretic active learning framework that guides the optimal selection of images from the unlabelled pool to be labeled based on maximizing the expected information gain (EIG) on an evaluation dataset.

extractions.description: The paper presents an active learning framework using information-theoretic methods to optimize the selection of medical images for labeling. It introduces an Adapted Expected Information Gain (AEIG) method to improve the efficiency of medical image classification, particularly dealing with class imbalance in datasets for diabetic retinopathy and skin lesions. The framework shows improved labeling efficiency by achieving high performance with significantly fewer labeled samples compared to traditional methods.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is on improving the labeling efficiency and accuracy of active learning methods in medical image classification. While it contributes to the medical field, sustainable development themes such as environmental impact or resource conservation are not the primary focus.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Large, annotated datasets are not widely available in medical image analysis due to the prohibitive time, costs, and challenges associated with labelling large datasets.

primary_category.justification: The paper's content focuses strictly on improving active learning methods for medical image classification, which is outside the direct scope of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
primary_category.quote: Experiments are performed on two different medical image classification datasets: multi-class diabetic retinopathy disease scale classification and multi-class skin lesion classification.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes identified in the paper.
secondary_categories.quote: This paper proposes an information-theoretic active learning framework that drives the selection of new image samples to label based on maximal information gain.
